info.title: dosbox-automation control API
info.description:
REST API for programmatic control of dosbox-automation. Automate installations, drive games, capture frames, and record or replay input.

The API is intended for local automation. By default the server binds to 127.0.0.1 and is not designed to be exposed to untrusted networks. Every endpoint under /api/v1 requires a bearer token; the documentation assets (this page, the landing page, openapi.json) are served without a token so the docs are browsable. Use the Authorize button to paste your token before running a request.

All endpoints read or write internal state atomically between emulated CPU steps. They never run during native DOS functions or interrupts, so the internal data structures are always consistent.

tags.name: Recording
tags.description: Capture and replay of input sequences.

tags.name: Drive
tags.description: Disk image mounting and disk swaps.

tags.name: Memory
tags.description: Memory read, write, allocate, and free.

tags.name: Batch
tags.description: Atomic multi-operation execution (memory, CPU, I/O port, freeze).

tags.name: Debug
tags.description: Interactive debugging: pause/step/continue, breakpoints, state inspection. Needs a debugger-enabled build - see capabilities.debugger in GET /api/v1/dosbox/info. Every route below returns 501 when it isn't.

tags.name: Wait
tags.description: Server-side long poll for a condition (text, screen change, frame count, memory value, debugger stop, script completion, program change) instead of client-side polling.

get.description: Returns the version string and a map of feature flags indicating which API groups are available. MCP clients use this to discover capabilities before calling endpoints.

features.description: Feature flags for API capability discovery.

get.summary: DOS data structures and MCB memory map
get.description: Returns pointers to internal DOS structures and walks the MCB chain to build a memory map of all allocated blocks.

200.description: List of lists, DOS swappable area, first shell, and MCB chain.

memoryMap.description: MCB chain walk. Each entry is one memory control block.

memoryMapTruncated.description: True if the chain walk stopped before a proper terminating block - either a hard cap of 1000 blocks was hit, or an invalid MCB type byte aborted it early. When true, memoryMap does not cover the whole chain.

get.summary: EMS (expanded memory) status and handle table
get.description: Guest-visible EMS state: whether the driver is enabled, total/free 16KB pages, and every active handle's name, page count, and current page-frame mapping. Distinct from mem/allocate?area=XMS, which is this API's own scratch allocator over the raw page pool, not the guest's EMS driver.

enabled.description: Whether the EMS driver is enabled for this session.

handles.description: Every currently active EMS handle (unused handle slots are omitted).

get.summary: XMS (extended memory) status and handle table
get.description: Guest-visible XMS state: free/largest-free KB, A20 line state, HMA/UMB ownership, and every currently allocated handle's size and lock count. Distinct from mem/allocate?area=XMS, which is this API's own scratch allocator over the raw page pool, not the guest's XMS driver.

enabled.description: Whether the XMS driver is enabled for this session.

totalKb.description: Total free extended memory in KB.

largestFreeKb.description: Largest contiguous free extended-memory block in KB.

handles.description: Every currently allocated XMS handle (free slots are omitted).

503.description: Allocation failed - either no free block was large enough, or the allocation registry (mem_allocations) is already at its entry cap.

get.description: Lists every allocation memory/allocate has made and not yet freed, plus free-memory totals for conventional, UMB, and XMS. Not part of dos/internals, which exists only to hand out pointers.

Reads `len` bytes from the given address. Parameters accept hex strings when prefixed with `0x`. The default response is raw binary; send `Accept: application/json` to get the data Base64-encoded in JSON.
Same as the unsegmented read. The segment may be a segment register name or a number.

put.description: Writes to the given address. Accepts raw bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` or a JSON object with a Base64 `data` field. The `If-Match` header (Base64) performs an atomic compare-and-swap and returns 412 when the current bytes do not match.

post.summary: Inject a sequence of input events
post.description: Returns immediately once the chain is armed (events_scheduled), before any of it has actually dispatched - use GET /input/replay/status to track progress, and DELETE /input/replay to cancel. Events with `t > 0` are scheduled via the PIC timer for cycle-accurate delivery; events carrying a `frame` field are scheduled against the frame counter instead. Returns 400 for unknown key names, event types, or button names, and 409 if a chain of the same kind (PIC-timed or frame-timed) is already running.

404.description: No recording by that name (only when 'recording' was given).

409.description: A replay chain of the same kind (PIC-timed or frame-timed) is already in progress.

get.summary: Read the DOS mouse driver's cursor position
get.description: The built-in INT 33h driver's own idea of where the cursor is, read directly from its state segment. driver_started is false - with x/y/buttons all defaulted - for a guest that never started the driver, one talking to the PS/2 or serial mouse directly instead (Windows 3.x, some protected-mode games), or one currently running Windows 3.x in 386 Enhanced mode: none of those have a readable position here.

post.summary: Warp the DOS mouse driver's cursor
post.description: Sets the INT 33h driver's cursor position directly (not through relative-motion accumulation), clamped to the driver's currently configured min/max range, then floored to the driver's position granularity (a multiple of a few pixels in most video modes, independent of any clamping), and fires a mouse-moved event so a registered guest callback runs and the cursor redraws. Returns the position actually applied, which can differ from the request even well inside the min/max range because of that granularity. 409 if the guest never started the driver, or is currently running Windows 3.x in 386 Enhanced mode.

409.description: The guest never started the INT 33h driver.

post.summary: Toggle pause on the active recording
Stop recording and return captured events
post.description: The returned events can be replayed via POST /input/sequence's 'events' array. Pass 'name' to also save the recording under that name for POST /input/sequence's 'recording' field - GET /input/recordings lists what's stored, DELETE /input/recordings/{name} removes one.

503.description: Named recording store is full (error_code registry_full); delete one first.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Save the recording under this name (<=64 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_-]) in the process-lifetime named recording store.

parameters.name: include_events
parameters.description: Only the literal value 'false' is special-cased and omits the 'events' array from the response body; any other value (or omitting the parameter) behaves the same as including it. Useful once the recording is also being saved by name, so the caller doesn't have to receive the full event list just to discard it.

get.description:
Returns the current frame. The format is chosen by the `format` query parameter or the `Accept` header. The `mode` parameter selects the source: `raw` (default) is the clean emulator framebuffer at native resolution, `rendered` is the post-shader image as shown on screen at window resolution. Neither includes the on-screen automation overlay (OSD). Returns 503 if no frame is available (raw: nothing rendered yet; rendered: nothing is being presented).

The raw format is a binary header (uint32 width, uint32 height, int32 pitch, uint8 pixel_format, uint16 palette_count) followed by palette data when paletted, then the image data.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Frame source: the emulator framebuffer or the rendered display.

get.description: Reads the text-mode character buffer and returns it as UTF-8, with CP437 box-drawing and shade glyphs preserved. Empty text with is_text_mode false in a graphics mode. Use this to drive installers by screen state instead of fixed timings.

post.summary: Mount or swap a disk image on a drive
post.description: Mount or swap a floppy or hard disk image on a drive letter. For multi-disk installs, call this when the installer prompts for the next disk. GET /mount/images lists what's available under the configured image roots; GET /mount/policy shows those roots and whether mounting is locked.

400.description: Rejected: a missing field, an invalid drive letter, or the image path failed mount policy. error_code is one of missing_field, invalid_drive_letter, does_not_resolve, not_regular_file, symlink_component, system_path, outside_whitelist, not_a_disk_image - see GET /mount/policy for the configured roots a policy-denied path must be under.

403.description: Mounting is locked (POST /mount/lock) - a one-way latch for the life of the process.

404.description: The resolved image path no longer exists (a race between validation and the mount itself).

500.description: The image passed mount policy validation but the drive itself failed to construct (unexpected image structure).

post.summary: Mount a host directory as a drive
post.description: Mount a host directory as a drive letter - the REST equivalent of the guest's own MOUNT command, directory form only (image files stay on POST /drive/swap). Mirrors an already-mounted letter the same way MOUNT itself does: it overwrites whatever was there, no unmount required first. GET /mount/policy shows the configured directory roots a policy-denied path must be under.

400.description: Rejected: a missing field, an invalid drive letter, the path isn't a directory, or it failed mount policy. error_code is one of missing_field, invalid_drive_letter, not_a_directory, does_not_resolve, symlink_component, system_path, outside_whitelist - see GET /mount/policy for the configured roots a policy-denied path must be under.

403.description: Mounting is locked (POST /mount/lock) - a one-way latch for the life of the process.

post.description: The request body is the Lua source. Loading replaces any previously loaded script.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A name for the script, used in status and logs.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Optional PRNG seed for deterministic runs.

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: Enable trace logging for this script.

400.description: No script loaded, or already running.

200.description: Script state. `output` mirrors the script's dosbox.output table when present.

compression.description: Present only if the request set a compression level.

409.description: A video capture is already running and the request tried to change the compression level.

mode.description: What feeds the encoder: 'raw' captures the emulator framebuffer at native resolution, 'rendered' captures the post-shader output at window resolution as shown on screen.

compression.description: Zlib compression level to apply to `mode` before starting, 0 (store only) to 9 (maximum). Set and started atomically in this one call; omit to keep the level already configured for `mode` (see GET /capture/video/compression).

path.description: Host filesystem path of the current (or, after a stop, the most recently finished) recording. Omitted if no video capture has run yet this session. Same disclosure decision as GET /drive's `info` field: this whole API sits behind the bearer token on loopback.

frames.description: Frames written so far (or, after a stop, in total). The clearest signal that a capture nominally ran but the emulator was paused or minimized the whole time: capturing:true with frames staying at 0.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds since the recording's file was created (not since capture/video/start was called - the file isn't created until the first frame arrives). Frozen at the final duration once the recording stops.

bytes_written.description: Bytes of video/audio chunk data written so far, or in total once stopped.

compression_level.description: Zlib level configured for `mode` at query time.

last_stop_reason.description: Why the most recent video capture ended. 'none' means no capture has ended yet; 'write_error' covers failed writes and a failed final flush; 'disk_space_low' means the recording was stopped cleanly before the capture drive ran out of space (capture_min_free_space_mb setting).

mode.description: Capture mode of the running recording, or of the most recently started one.

get.description: Zlib compression levels applied when the next video capture starts, one per capture mode. 0 is store only, 9 is maximum compression.

put.description: Sets the zlib compression level for one or both capture modes. Takes effect when the next capture starts. Rejected while a video capture is running, because the running capture keeps the level it started with.

200.description: Applied compression levels for both modes.

post.summary: Type a string with paced key injection
post.description: Translates each character to its key equivalent and injects them paced to avoid overflowing the keyboard buffer. The optional cps parameter controls characters per second. Maximum 4096 characters per call.

409.description: Injection failed (e.g. another type in progress).

post.description: Scans a memory range for all occurrences of a value. The width selects byte (1), word (2), or dword (4) matching. Maximum scan span is 16 MB. 'matches' is capped at 'limit' (default 256, max 4096); 'total' reports the real match count even when it exceeds that, and 'truncated' says whether it did.

matches.description: Physical addresses where the value was found, up to 'limit' entries.

total.description: The real number of matches, which can exceed matches.length.

post.summary: Scan memory for a masked byte signature
post.description: Scans a memory range for a masked byte signature, e.g. Ghidra's copyable byte string '8B 46 ?? 50 E8': space-separated hex-pair bytes and '??' wildcards, 1-256 tokens, at least one fixed byte. Maximum scan span is 16 MB. Rejected with 400 when the pattern isn't selective enough for the requested span (too many wildcards would make it match almost everywhere) or when its fixed-byte count is too high for the span (would risk exceeding the scan time budget). 'matches' is capped at 'limit' (default 256, max 4096); 'total' reports the real match count even when it exceeds that, and 'truncated' says whether it did. If an execute breakpoint is active inside the range, the scan reads through its 0xCC trap byte to the real instruction underneath.

matches.description: Physical addresses where the pattern's first byte matched, up to 'limit' entries.

total.description: The real number of matches, which can exceed matches.length.

post.summary: Capture a memory range for later comparison
post.description: Captures [start, end) (max 16 MB) so it can be compared against later with POST /memory/diff - the first step of a snapshot-and-refine workflow for locating an unknown value's address. Returns a handle. Snapshots are capped by total bytes across every live snapshot (32 MB, LRU-evicted, not capped by count), plus a backstop cap on the number of live snapshots.

post.summary: Compare current memory against a snapshot and narrow the candidates
post.description: Compares current guest memory against a memory/snapshot handle and narrows it to whatever satisfies 'op'. The first diff call on a handle compares the whole captured range against fresh memory; every call after that re-checks only the addresses that survived the previous call, so repeated calls on the same handle progressively refine - each call re-baselines, so 'increased' means increased since the *previous* diff call, not the original snapshot. 'width' (1, 2, or 4 bytes, default 1) is only settable on a handle's first diff call and locks in from then on; a later call that names a different width is rejected. A handle that narrows to zero candidates is removed - the next diff on it, or on any handle that doesn't currently exist, fails with 404.

total.description: The real number of survivors this round, which can exceed matches.length.

candidates.description: How many addresses are being tracked for the next diff call on this handle. Can be less than total if there were more true survivors than the registry's per-handle candidate cap (65536) - the ones kept are an arbitrary subset, so treat a heavily-truncated round as a signal to narrow the search and take a new snapshot rather than trusting the survivors.

404.description: No snapshot with that handle (never existed, evicted, or already narrowed to zero candidates).

post.description: Pins a memory location to a fixed value. The value is rewritten every emulation frame. Calling again with the same address updates the frozen value.

delete.description: With no body or without an address field, clears all freezes. With an address field, removes only that one.

address.description: Remove only this freeze. Omit to clear all.

get.description: Reads a byte or word from an I/O port. The port number accepts hex with a 0x prefix.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Port number (0x0000..0xFFFF). Hex with 0x prefix accepted.

put.description: Writes a byte or word to an I/O port.
Sets a general-purpose or segment register. General registers: eax, ebx, ecx, edx, esi, edi, esp, ebp. Segment registers: cs, ds, es, ss, fs, gs (values must be 0..0xFFFF).

post.summary: Execute a batch of memory/CPU/port/freeze operations atomically
post.description: Applies 1-64 memory, CPU register, I/O port, and freeze operations in order, in a single pass on the emulation thread - no other request can interleave mid-batch. Not a transaction: there is no rollback, only in-order application and (with on_error='abort', the default) an early stop once one op fails. Every op that was attempted gets a result; every op skipped by an abort gets status 'skipped'. Op count and per-batch byte budgets are deliberately tighter than the equivalent single-op routes - see /api/v1/dosbox/info's capabilities.batch.

200.description: Per-op results, index-correlated with the request's 'ops'.

aborted.description: True when on_error='abort' stopped the batch before every op was attempted.

get.summary: List all drive letters and what's mounted on each
get.description: Walks A: through Z:, reporting which are mounted and, for each mounted one, its type and host info. The read side drive/swap never had: which letters are free to swap something onto.

Whether mounting is locked, and the directory/image roots an API-origin mount must be under. An empty allowed_image_roots means every drive/swap call is refused by policy regardless of path - the out-of-the-box state until an operator configures mount_allowed_image_roots.

get.summary: List image files under the configured image roots
get.description: Non-recursive per-root listing of regular files under mount_allowed_image_roots, so an agent can discover what's mountable without shell access. Each entry's path is independently re-validated against the same policy drive/swap enforces, so a path returned here will not then be refused by mount policy (it can still fail structural validation as a disk image).

A finished, cancelled, or self-aborted chain keeps reporting its final total/dispatched/elapsed_ms/drift_ms rather than zeroing them out - checking status right after a replay ends is the normal sequence.

delete.description: Drains both the PIC-timed and frame-timed chains unconditionally, whichever (if either) is active. Safe to call when nothing is running - reports cancelled:false rather than erroring.

get.description: Metadata only, process-lifetime and in-memory - nothing here survives a restart. Use POST /input/sequence {"recording": "<name>"} to replay one.
stop mirrors the most recently published DebugStop record, whether or not the emulator is stopped right now.

200.description: Whether the debugger is currently stopped, and the last stop record.

post.description: Idempotent: pausing an already-paused emulator returns status 'ok' again rather than an error.

200.description: Resumed. The next stop (if any) happens asynchronously - poll GET /debug/wait?since_stop_id=resumed_from_stop_id.

post.description: Optional JSON body: {"count": N} to step N instructions in one call (default 1). N is bounded; see debug.h's DEBUG_MaxStepCount.

200.description: Stepped. status is 'not_paused' when the emulator wasn't stopped to begin with.

Armed a one-shot breakpoint past the current instruction, or fell back to a plain step when the current instruction isn't one of call/int/loop/rep. stop is only present when a step was published synchronously by this call - otherwise poll GET /debug/wait?since_stop_id=resumed_from_stop_id.
Armed a one-shot breakpoint at segment:offset and resumed. The actual stop happens asynchronously - poll GET /debug/wait?since_stop_id=resumed_from_stop_id.

post.summary: Run until the current function returns
post.description: Backtraces (heuristically, real mode has no reliable frame pointer chain) to the caller's return address and plants a one-shot breakpoint there.

200.description: status is 'no_confident_caller_frame' when the backtrace couldn't resolve a caller to aim at (nothing is armed in that case), or 'not_paused' when the emulator wasn't stopped. On 'ok', poll GET /debug/wait?since_stop_id=resumed_from_stop_id for the actual stop.

get.summary: Long-poll for the next debugger stop
get.description: Blocks the calling connection (not a Bridge command, so it never holds the emulation thread) until a stop newer than since_stop_id is published or timeout_ms elapses.

parameters.name: since_stop_id
parameters.description: Return immediately if the current stop_id already exceeds this.

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Bounded by wait.min_timeout_ms/max_timeout_ms in GET /dosbox/info's limits block.

200.description: Either a new stop past since_stop_id, or a timeout with the live debugging state.

get.description: Real-mode-style seg:off addressing, decoded with the live CS's current operand-size default - not a protected-mode GDT resolution. Always available, regardless of the debugger capability.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Bounded by disassemble.max_count in GET /dosbox/info's limits block.

200.description: Decoded instructions. truncated is true when count instructions would have read past the end of emulated memory.

get.summary: Walk the call stack from the current frame
get.description: Heuristic in DOS real mode: expect most walks to resolve confidently one or two frames before confidence drops. Always available, regardless of the debugger capability.

parameters.name: max_frames
parameters.description: Bounded by backtrace.max_frames in GET /dosbox/info's limits block; defaults to backtrace.default_frames.

200.description: Frames from innermost outward. confidence is 'low' once BP stops looking like a real frame-pointer chain - real-mode DOS code has no guarantee it kept one at all.

post.description: type is 'execute', 'interrupt', or 'memory'. execute/memory take segment+offset; interrupt takes int (0x00-0xFF) and optional ah/al (omit for wildcard). Optional: once (bool), ignore_count (int, mutually exclusive with once), condition (BreakpointCondition, mutually exclusive with once). memory breakpoints additionally need a heavy-debugger build - see capabilities.debugger in GET /dosbox/info - and return 501 otherwise even when C_DEBUGGER is on. memory breakpoints additionally accept an optional 'trigger' ('write', the default, or 'read').

trigger.description: Only used when type is 'memory'. 'write' (default) matches the console's BPM command; 'read' matches BPMR.

200.description: Created. Echoes back the stored breakpoint, including the id and index the engine assigned.

409.description: A breakpoint already exists at this location and either it or this one carries an ignore_count or condition - only the first match in list order is ever evaluated, so the second would silently never fire. List existing breakpoints and delete the conflicting one first.

delete.description: Body is optional. Specify exactly one of 'id' or 'index' to delete a single breakpoint; omit the body (or send an empty one) to delete all.

200.description: Deleted. An empty body deletes all breakpoints (status 'cleared'); a body with 'id' or 'index' deletes just that one (status 'removed').

404.description: No breakpoint at the given id/index.

get.description: value/hasValue are read live from guest memory at request time, not cached - matches the interactive debugger's own variable panel refresh.

post.description: name is capped at 15 characters. segment:offset resolves to a flat address at add time, the same way the interactive IV console command does - matches the console's own IV command, exposed for automation.

200.description: Created. Echoes back the stored watch, including its live value.

delete.description: Body is optional. Specify 'address' to delete a single watch; omit the body (or send an empty one) to delete all.

200.description: Deleted. An empty body deletes all watches (status 'cleared'); a body with 'address' deletes just that one (status 'removed').

404.description: No watch at the given address.

get.summary: Read the debug log of the loaded script
get.description: Only available for a script started with debug=true (POST /script/load). Reads the last script.max_log_tail_bytes of the file directly, independent of the emulation thread.

200.description: Tail of the debug log, up to script.max_log_tail_bytes.

400.description: No debug script is loaded - the currently loaded script (if any) wasn't started with debug=true.

404.description: A debug script is loaded but its log either failed to open on the engine side, or isn't readable now.

post.description: One request, one wait: blocks the calling connection (never the emulation thread) until the condition named by 'for' is satisfied or timeout_ms elapses. 'for' is one of text, screen_change, frames, replay_done, memory, stopped, script_done, program, each taking its own extra fields - see the engine's wait.h for the full per-condition field list. reason on return is 'matched', 'timeout', 'emulator_stopped' (a frame-driven condition can't progress while paused), 'shutting_down', or 'error'.

timeout_ms.description: Bounded by wait.min_timeout_ms/max_timeout_ms in GET /dosbox/info's limits block.

baseline_hash.description: 'screen_change' condition: 16 hex chars, from a prior text_hash/hash value.

count.description: 'frames' condition: how many frames from now.

200.description: The wait ended, either satisfied or on timeout/error - both are 200, not an HTTP-level failure. Extra fields beyond satisfied/reason/for depend on which condition was requested (e.g. text_hash for 'text', frame for 'frames', value for 'memory').

get.description: The only route that answers without a bearer token (see the security scheme description). Lets a bridge check version and protocol compatibility before it has - or can even obtain - a token. Returns exactly these three fields: no pid, uptime, features, or anything else that would need per-instance state.

mcp_protocol.description: Highest dosbox-mcp wire protocol minor this build implements, as major.minor.

bearerAuth.description: The API token, written to the token file at startup by default (see webserver_token_file), or supplied via DOSBOX_API_TOKEN. The log only ever gets a short preview. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

MemorySegment.name: segment
MemorySegment.description: Segment register name or a number. Hex allowed with a 0x prefix.

MemoryOffset.name: offset
MemoryOffset.description: Address offset. Hex allowed with a 0x prefix.

MemoryLen.name: len
MemoryLen.description: Number of bytes to read. Hex allowed with a 0x prefix.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: Base64-encoded expected current bytes for an atomic compare-and-swap.

DebuggerNotBuilt.description: The debugger capability isn't built into this binary (C_DEBUGGER=0). See capabilities.debugger in GET /api/v1/dosbox/info.

example.error: debug_status: debugger capability not built in this binary

error_code.description: Stable machine-readable cause, additive to 'error'. Not present on every error response.

retryable.description: Whether the same request might succeed unmodified after waiting. Not present on every error response.

Registers.description: 32-bit general registers, EIP, flags, and 16-bit segment registers.

strategy.description: Defaults to BEST_FIT if omitted. The XMS allocator only supports BEST_FIT.

MemoryAllocations.description: Free-memory totals plus every allocation this API has made and not yet freed.

addr.description: Physical address, as returned by memory/allocate.

size.description: Bytes actually reserved (paragraph/page-rounded), not necessarily the exact size requested.

conventionalFreeBytes.description: Total free conventional memory, summed across every free MCB block.

conventionalLargestBlockBytes.description: The single largest free conventional block - what actually bounds the next allocation, since a request larger than this fails even if conventionalFreeBytes is bigger.

conventionalTruncated.description: True if the conventional MCB chain walk was cut short (cap or corrupt chain) - the free-byte totals above may then be an undercount.

umbFreeBytes.description: Total free upper memory block space, 0 if no UMB chain is linked.

umbTruncated.description: Same meaning as conventionalTruncated, for the UMB chain walk.

xmsFreeBytes.description: Free space in the page allocator pool the XMS area allocates from.

InputEvent.description: One input event. Unknown fields are rejected with a 400 naming the allowed fields for the event type.

t.description: Absolute position on the sequence timeline in milliseconds (recording format). Mutually exclusive with 'delay_ms'.

key.description: Key name, e.g. KBD_enter. Used by key events.

pressed.description: Press (true) or release (false). Used by key and mouse_button events.

x_rel.description: Horizontal mouse delta in pixels, positive right (mouse_move events). Ignored if 'x_abs'/'y_abs' are also given on the same event.

y_rel.description: Relative Y motion. Used by mouse_move.

delay_ms.description: Wait this many milliseconds after the previous event before firing (relative timing; the natural form for hand-written sequences). Mutually exclusive with 't'.

frame.description: Frame number for frame-locked replay (recording format).

x_abs.description: Warp the DOS mouse driver's cursor to this exact guest pixel X position (mouse_move events) - the same closed loop as POST /input/mouse, folded into a sequence event. Must be given together with 'y_abs', or not at all; when given, 'x_rel'/'y_rel' on the same event are ignored. No effect if the guest never started the INT 33h driver (see GET /input/mouse's driver_started).

driver_started.description: False if the guest never started the INT 33h driver, or is currently running Windows 3.x in 386 Enhanced mode - x/y/buttons are then all defaulted, not meaningful.

RecordedInputEvent.description: The shape of one entry in RecordingResult.events (GET/POST .../record/stop?include_events=true) - a recorded event as captured, not a request body. Shares most fields with InputEvent, but a recorded mouse_move's absolute position is host window pixels at record time (host_x_abs/host_y_abs), a different coordinate space from InputEvent's 'x_abs'/'y_abs' (guest DOS screen pixels) - deliberately different field names, so reposting a dump verbatim as a /input/sequence body can't silently warp the cursor to the wrong place.

host_x_abs.description: Host window pixel X position at record time. Diagnostic only - not the coordinate space InputEvent's 'x_abs' expects.

host_y_abs.description: Host window pixel Y position at record time. See 'host_x_abs'.

recording.description: Name of a stored recording (see GET /input/recordings) to replay instead of an inline 'events' array. Mutually exclusive with 'events' - provide exactly one.

truncated.description: True if MaxInputEvents (32000) was hit during this recording and further events were dropped.

name.description: Present only if the stop request named this recording.

truncated.description: True if MaxInputEvents was hit and further events are being dropped.

is_text_mode.description: False in graphics modes; text is empty then.

columns.description: Live column count from the BIOS data area.

text.description: Screen contents, rows separated by newlines, CP437 converted to UTF-8.

error.description: Present only when the script errored.

output.description: The script's dosbox.output table, when set.

output_truncated.description: True when dosbox.output was too large or deeply nested and was cut off - see capabilities.script.limits in GET /api/v1/dosbox/info. Always present.

log_path.description: Present only when the loaded script was started with debug=true. GET /script/log reads it.

start.description: Physical start address of the scan range.

end.description: Physical end address (exclusive). Max span 16 MB.

limit.description: Max matches to return, 1-4096. The full match count is still reported in 'total' even when it exceeds this.

pattern.description: Space-separated hex-pair bytes and '??' wildcards, e.g. '8B 46 ?? 50 E8'. 1-256 tokens, at least one fixed byte.

start.description: Physical start address of the scan range.

end.description: Physical end address (exclusive). Max span 16 MB.

limit.description: Max matches to return, 1-4096. The full match count is still reported in 'total' even when it exceeds this.

start.description: Physical start address of the range to capture.

end.description: Physical end address (exclusive). Max span 16 MB.

op.description: How to compare each candidate's current value to the value recorded for it. 'equals' is a synonym for 'unchanged'.

width.description: Comparison width in bytes. Only settable on a handle's first diff call - locked in from then on.

limit.description: Max matches to return, 1-4096. The full survivor count is still reported in 'total' even when it exceeds this.

McbBlock.description: One DOS Memory Control Block from the MCB chain.

type.description: M for middle, Z for last block.

pspSegment.description: PSP segment of the owning process.

filename.description: Owner filename from the MCB header.

isLast.description: True if this is the last block in the chain.

name.description: The handle's DOS-assigned name, up to 8 characters (empty if never set).

pageMappings.description: Which of this handle's logical pages are currently mapped into the page frame.

logicalPage.description: This handle's own page number mapped into that slot.

lockCount.description: How many times this block is currently locked.

info.description: Present only when mounted. The mounted host path for local/FAT/ISO/CD-ROM drives - a filesystem path disclosure, deliberate: this whole API sits behind the bearer token on loopback.

drives.description: Always 26 entries, A through Z, in order.

allowed_image_roots.description: Image-file roots (drive/swap, IMGMOUNT via the API origin), canonicalized. Empty means every API-origin image mount is refused, regardless of path.

path.description: Full canonical host path - usable directly as drive/swap's 'image'.

truncated.description: True if this root held more regular files than the max_images_per_root cap (see dosbox/info's capabilities.drive.limits).

engine.description: Which dispatch engine the reported numbers describe. "mixed" only happens if two separate POST calls armed one chain of each kind at once; "none" means no replay has run yet this session.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock time since the chain started. Live while active; frozen at its final value once the chain finishes, is cancelled, or self-aborts (see capabilities.input.limits.replay_stall_threshold_ms).

drift_ms.description: Wall-clock drift (actual minus expected) of the most recently dispatched event.

BatchOp.description: One operation. 'op' selects the shape of the rest: mem_read (segment?, offset, len), mem_write (segment?, offset, data), mem_cas (segment?, offset, data, expected), cpu_read (), cpu_write (register, value), port_read (port, width?), port_write (port, width?, value), freeze_set (address, value, width?), freeze_clear (address).

segment.description: mem_read/mem_write/mem_cas only. Register name (cs/ds/es/fs/gs/ss, resolved live at execution time) or a fixed paragraph value 0x0000..0xFFFF. Omit for a plain linear offset.

offset.description: mem_read/mem_write/mem_cas only. Segment-relative if 'segment' is given, otherwise a linear physical offset.

data.description: mem_write/mem_cas only. Base64-encoded bytes to write.

expected.description: mem_cas only. Base64-encoded bytes the address must currently hold for the write to happen.

register.description: cpu_write only. Register name (eax, ebx, ecx, edx, esi, edi, esp, ebp, cs, ds, es, ss, fs, gs).

width.description: port_read/port_write (1 or 2, default 1) or freeze_set (1, 2, or 4, default 1).

ops.description: 1-64 operations, applied in order in a single atomic pass on the emulation thread. Total mem_read length across the batch is capped at 1 MiB, total mem_write/mem_cas data+expected at 256 KiB.

on_error.description: 'abort' (default) stops applying further ops once one fails (mem_cas conflict, freeze_set registry full, freeze_clear not found, or an out-of-range register-relative address) - the ops after it are reported 'skipped', not attempted. 'continue' applies every op regardless.

addr.description: mem_read/mem_write/mem_cas, when status is ok or conflict.

data.description: Base64. mem_read (the bytes read) or mem_cas conflict (the actual current bytes).

width.description: freeze_set only, when status is ok.

BreakpointCondition.description: Extra match condition on a breakpoint, evaluated only once the breakpoint's own location/int-ah-al already matched. Either register-based (register/op/value) or memory-based (segment/offset/width/op/value), never both. Absent or null means the breakpoint always stops.

width.description: Memory-based condition: value width in bytes.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique for the life of the process.

index.description: Current position in the breakpoint list; not stable across deletes.

ah.description: interrupt breakpoints only; DEBUG_BPINT_ANY (0x100) means wildcard.

al.description: interrupt breakpoints only; DEBUG_BPINT_ANY (0x100) means wildcard.

once.description: Removed automatically after its first hit.

ignore_count.description: Remaining hits to skip before this breakpoint actually stops.

DebugStop.description: A snapshot of emulator state at the moment execution paused - on a breakpoint hit, an explicit pause, or after a step.

stop_id.description: Monotonically increasing; poll GET /debug/wait?since_stop_id= for the next one.

code_bytes.description: A few bytes at CS:EIP, base64-encoded.

breakpoint.description: The breakpoint that caused this stop, or null when the stop wasn't a breakpoint hit.
